community engagement is not only a matter of doing good for others, but also of doing well for oneself.

In summary, our research is concerned with
how universities can best respond to the call to be socially responsible.
the question: how do universities in South Africa engage with the communities that surround them?
the question of how to make the university more relevant to society.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the university’s role in the development of the community is not a new phenomenon.
universities must ‘promot and develop social responsibility’.
the university is a community of scholars and students who engage with the community in the search for knowledge and the application of knowledge to solve problems in society.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
community engagement, as it is understood and practised in the South African context, has not yet been able to realise its full potential.
we are in search of a developmental University.
universities must be more than a place of learning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the notion of a university that is committed to the community is not a new idea, but one that has been around for a very long time and has been articulated in various ways.
universities should be more than just ‘engaging’ with their surrounding communities; they should be ‘developing’ them.
community engagement is not a panacea for the problems of higher education in South Africa; nor is it the only means of enhancing the relevance of universities.
